world.rationale: AI capability trends (multi-hour METR horizons in 2026, collapsing solar and battery costs) make superintelligence by 2050 roughly a coin flip and likely by 2100. If it arrives, loss of control or AI-enabled disempowerment dominates doom, with AI-amplified bio and great-power war as secondary routes, but SI also makes 90% global access to the essentials plausible. Without SI, doom is mostly tail risk from nuclear war and engineered pandemics, since climate and resource stress hurt badly but rarely end civilization; global abundance stays unlikely because Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, a large share of 2100 humanity, are far below the health and security thresholds.

countries.rationale: France already meets nearly all essentials, with a nuclear-heavy grid, low water stress and high life expectancy, so its collapse risk is mostly global doom plus a European war tail. Abundance is limited by affordability and food insecurity (9.4% moderate or severe), aging and social grievance rather than by physical capacity.

Enormous wealth and resource base make physical collapse unlikely outside global catastrophe, but the US is the likely SI frontier and a nuclear target. Political polarization, uneven health-care access, a lower life expectancy than peers and gun violence weigh on abundance and the security pillar.

Strong state capacity, universal electricity and dominance of clean-energy supply chains support abundance, but a Taiwan or US-China AI-race war is the main collapse route. Northern water stress, food-import dependence and a fertility rate near 1.0 driving rapid aging are the main slow-burn risks.

Extremely high water stress, groundwater depletion and growing wet-bulb heat exposure threaten water and food, and a nuclear-armed rivalry with Pakistan adds a security tail. Fast growth and near-universal electricity give a credible path to abundance, but the 90% threshold for safe water and life expectancy of 75 or more is a high bar.

Very high fragility (FSI 96.6), insurgency and banditry, 76.5% moderate or severe food insecurity and a life expectancy of 54.6 leave little buffer, while the population may roughly double by 2100. Abundance without SI is very unlikely; SI could leapfrog health and energy but also disrupt oil revenue and labor markets.

Brazil is a food and hydro-energy surplus country with low water stress and no major interstate threats, so collapse is unlikely outside global doom. High criminal violence, inequality and Amazon tipping-point risk to rainfall are what keep abundance well short of certain.

A dense, low-lying delta exposed to accelerating sea-level rise, cyclones, salinization and upstream water control makes water and food the main collapse routes. Strong development gains and near-universal electricity help, but high climate vulnerability and low adaptive readiness limit abundance.

Near-total dependence on the Nile (water stress 4.85) and on wheat imports, a growing population and Delta exposure to sea-level rise make water and food the binding pillars. Cheap solar-powered desalination, much more likely with SI, is the main route to abundance; regional conflict and fiscal fragility add security risk.
